replacements.old: Louisiana is reported in 2026 sources as having a Medigap birthday rule. Reports describe a window of about 63 days following your birthday to switch to a plan with equal or lesser benefits without health questions, with the choice generally limited to your current insurer or its affiliate, though one guide describes a different window, so the details vary by source. Confirm the current window and rules with the Louisiana Department of Insurance before relying on it.
replacements.new: Louisiana has a Medigap birthday rule, set in state law. If you already have a Medigap policy, you get a yearly open enrollment period. It starts on your birthday and lasts 63 calendar days. During it you can buy a Medigap policy from your current insurer or one of its affiliates. If the plan you pick has benefits equal to or less than your current plan, the insurer cannot turn you down or charge you more because of your health. Source: Louisiana Revised Statutes 22:1112, read November 2026. The same law gives a 63-day window to people without a Medigap policy who had health coverage through their own employer when they became eligible for Medicare. It starts when that plan ends, stops providing some or all health benefits, or when they leave it, and it covers the plan letters that federal law guarantees at first Medicare eligibility. For free, unbiased help, Louisiana’s counseling program is LaSHIP, run by the Louisiana Department of Insurance.

Confirm the current rule with the West Virginia Offices of the Insurance Commissioner before relying on it, and do not cancel your current plan until a new one is approved.
replacements.new:
West Virginia has a Medigap birthday rule. It comes from House Bill 4869, a 2026 state law that took effect June 11, 2026. If your Medigap policy has been continuously in force for at least 24 months, you can replace it once per calendar year. The application period begins on the first day of the month of your birthday and ends 60 days later. The new policy must come from the same insurer or an affiliated insurer, and it must have the same or fewer standardized benefits. For that replacement the insurer may not turn you down, use medical underwriting, or add a pre-existing condition exclusion or waiting period. If neither your insurer nor an affiliate has accepted applications for such a plan for at least 12 months, you may buy one from any insurer authorized to sell Medigap in West Virginia. A replacement policy must itself be in force for 24 months before you can replace it again. The same law gives a guaranteed issue right to people 65 or older who are entitled to Medicare and lose Medicaid eligibility. Source: West Virginia Insurance Bulletin No. 26-02, Offices of the Insurance Commissioner, issued April 8, 2026, read November 2026.

West Virginia’s Medicare supplement rule also gives you a six-month open enrollment period. It starts the first month you are both 65 or older and enrolled in Part B. During those six months an insurer cannot turn you down or charge you more because of your health. Source: West Virginia Code of State Rules 114-24, effective June 1, 2025, read November 2026. Rules can change, so confirm with the West Virginia Offices of the Insurance Commissioner, and do not cancel your current plan until a new one is approved.

"The guaranteed issue right set forth in the bill is available if the individual's existing Medigap policy has been continuously in force for at least 24 months as of the effective date of the replacement policy. Each replacement policy is subject to the same 24-month continuous coverage requirement before it may be replaced again." "an individual who is enrolled in a Medigap policy has a guaranteed issue right once per calendar year to replace that policy. The guaranteed issue application period begins on the first day of the month of the individual's birthday and ends 60 days thereafter. "the insurer may not deny issuance, impose medical underwriting or impose a pre-existing condition exclusion or waiting period." "an individual has a guaranteed issue right to purchase a Medigap policy who is 65 years of age or older on the date the individual's Medicaid eligibility ends, is entitled to Medicare and loses eligibility for medical assistance under Medicaid." replacements.new: You can apply any time of year. You can switch without health questions during your six-month Medigap Open Enrollment Period, in federal guaranteed-issue situations, and under the West Virginia birthday rule. Under that rule, if your policy has been in force at least 24 months, once per calendar year you can replace it with a plan that has the same or fewer benefits from the same insurer or an affiliate. The application period begins on the first day of your birthday month and ends 60 days later. Confirm current rules with the West Virginia Offices of the Insurance Commissioner.
